read.instructionDe: Lesen Sie die Information am Bahnhof. Tippen Sie auf ein Wort für seine Bedeutung.
read.instructionEn: Read the notice at the station. Tap a word for its meaning.
read.text:
Bus am Bahnhof Bremen
Sie haben kein Auto? Fahren Sie mit dem Bus!
In welches Land fahren Sie?
Deutschland: Der Bus fährt heute und morgen nach Berlin.
Österreich: Der Bus fährt nächste Woche am Montag.
In die Schweiz fährt der Bus leider nicht.
Abfahrt: immer um 8 Uhr, hier am Bahnhof.
Die Fahrkarte kaufen Sie beim Fahrer oder bei der Fahrerin.

questions.promptDe: Wann fährt der Bus nach Österreich? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
questions.promptEn: When does the bus go to Austria? Choose the answer.
options: Today and tomorrow.
Next week, on Monday.
Next week, on Friday.
questions.explanationDe: In der Information steht: Österreich – der Bus fährt nächste Woche am Montag. Heute und morgen fährt er nach Berlin.
questions.explanationEn: The notice says the bus to Austria runs next week, on Monday. Today and tomorrow it goes to Berlin.

questions.promptDe: Wo kaufen Sie die Fahrkarte für den Bus? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
questions.promptEn: Where do you buy the ticket for the bus? Choose the answer.
options: At the counter in the station.
From a machine at the platform.
From the driver of the bus.
questions.answer: From the driver of the bus.
questions.explanationDe: In der Information steht: Die Fahrkarte kaufen Sie beim Fahrer oder bei der Fahrerin.
questions.explanationEn: The notice says you buy the ticket from the driver: a man (Fahrer) or a woman (Fahrerin).

meaning.promptDe: Wann und wo fährt der Zug nach Österreich? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
meaning.promptEn: When and where does the train to Austria leave? Choose the answer.
options: At four o’clock from platform nine.
At nine o’clock from platform five.
At nine o’clock from platform four.
meaning.answer: At nine o’clock from platform four.

meaning.promptDe: Was sagt Herr Schmidt über den Zug? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: What does Herr Schmidt say about the train? Choose the meaning.
options: The train is on time.
The train is delayed.
The train is full.

meaning.promptDe: Was kostet die Fahrkarte? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
meaning.promptEn: How much is the ticket? Choose the answer.
options: Twenty euros.
Fifteen euros.
Fifty euros.

meaning.promptDe: Ist das Gleis weit? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: Is the platform far? Choose the meaning.
options: No, the train leaves right here, from platform four.
Yes, platform four is at the other end of the station.
No, but Ana has to take the bus to get there.
meaning.answer: No, the train leaves right here, from platform four.

meaning.promptDe: Was sagt die Durchsage? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: What does the announcement say? Choose the meaning.
options: The train is on time; please board at platform four.
The train is cancelled; please take the bus.
The train is delayed; please change at platform five.
meaning.answer: The train is delayed; please change at platform five.

nextHook.de: Im Kurs fragt Lena Tim: Was hast du gestern gemacht? Und für Freitag haben die beiden einen Plan.
nextHook.en: In class, Lena asks Tim what he did yesterday. And the two of them have a plan for Friday.

notes: Chunks are the five question-answer pairs (Ana asks, Herr Schmidt answers). Ana opens every pair, so each say line (0, 2, 4, 6, 8) is the first line of its chunk and the say screen has no cue line before it (SceneStage only takes a cue from an earlier line of the same chunk). The alternative, 3-line chunks that end on Ana's next question, would cut every exchange in the middle; I did not do that. None of the say lines is a dictation line (1, 9).

Read text: a bus line's notice at Bremen station. It carries all eight Wortfeld entries the dialogue lacks (Fahrer, Fahrerin, Deutschland, Bahnhof, Land, morgen, nächste Woche, Auto) and agrees with the dialogue: the bus does not go to Switzerland (dialogue lines 6–7, zero-based), and the train facts (nine o'clock, platform four) are not touched.

Hard to fit: das Land (a station notice has little use for the bare word; it stands in the heading question „In welches Land fahren Sie?“, with Deutschland and Österreich as the two answers below it) and the pair Fahrer/Fahrerin (carried by the real bus-sign phrase „Fahrkarte beim Fahrer“, here „beim Fahrer oder bei der Fahrerin“). das Auto stands in the notice's opening pitch.
The gloss finder needs „Fahrer“ and „Fahrerin“ as separate whitespace tokens, so the usual form-style „Fahrer/Fahrerin“ would not count; hence „beim Fahrer oder bei der Fahrerin“.

Existing data, dialogue lines 6–7 (zero-based): Ana asks two unrelated questions in one line („Fährt der Bus auch in die Schweiz? Ist das Gleis weit?“) and Herr Schmidt's „Nein, leider nicht.“ can be read as the answer to either. My meaning question for that chunk asks only about the platform, which his second sentence answers unambiguously.

Existing data, dialogue lines 8–9 (zero-based): Ana's question „Und wann ist die Ankunft?“ is never answered; the next line is the announcement. And line 3 says the train is on time while line 9 announces a delay. As a plot turn that works, but nothing marks it as one.

Existing data, dialogue line 9: „Bitte an Gleis fünf umsteigen!“ reads oddly to me: umsteigen is changing trains, and a platform change is normally announced as „Der Zug fährt heute von Gleis fünf“. The meaning option follows the course's own English („please change at platform five“). Please have a native reviewer decide.
Phonetik: all three items are sentence-melody items (Ja/Nein-Frage, rising, with an arrow), not word-stress items, so the sound stage is pending for L10. Not changed.

PROOF (added 2026-11-14): four tasks, one per can-do, in can-do order. The German prompts are cue dialogues („Sie: …“) without an instruction verb, because RULE 35 holds promptDe to the taught-word horizon; the English twin carries the instruction. The partners have no name („Ein Mann arbeitet am Bahnhof“, „Der Fahrer“): the engine removes a final „, Herr Schmidt“ but not a leading „Herr Schmidt, …“ (engine limit 3).

Proof goal 0 (ask when the train leaves): one part, a when-question: „Wann“ or „Um wie viel Uhr“ + „fährt der Zug (nach Österreich)?“ or „ist die Abfahrt?“; also with geht or kommt (pool item extra-a11-l10-01 and the pretest accept both for the train), after „Entschuldigung, “, before „, bitte“, and with the dialogue’s „Und wann …“. LIMIT: the dialogue never asks when the train leaves. Line 0 (zero-based) asks whether it goes, line 8 asks „wann ist die Ankunft?“; the learner combines wann (Lektion 8) with line 0. Re-teach: lines 0 and 8; line 8 copied with its „Danke!“ fails (engine limit 1). „Wann fährt der Zug ab?“ cannot be accepted: RULE 35 reports „ab“ as untaught. „Wann fahrt der Zug?“ fails: the checker reads fährt/fahrt as conjugation, as the notice does.

Proof goal 1 (ask for the price of a ticket): one part: „Was kostet / Wie viel kostet / Wie teuer ist + die Fahrkarte / eine Fahrkarte (nach Österreich)?“ (the Lektion 4 forms), or the Lektion’s own yes/no question of line 4 with the money the cue gives: „Kostet die/eine Fahrkarte (nach Österreich) zwanzig Euro / 20 Euro / 20 €?“; also after „Entschuldigung, “ and, for the W-questions, before „, bitte“. Re-teach: dialogue line 4, which passes as it stands. Refused on purpose: another amount („fünfzehn Euro“), another destination, and „Was kostet das?“ (the ticket is not named).

Proof goal 2 (understand announcements): multiple_choice. LIMIT: this is a listening can-do, but a proof choice task has no audio field, so the announcement is printed in the prompt and read, not heard. It is a new announcement, not dialogue line 9. Four German options, two by two: on time or not, platform five or platform ten (ten is the hour in the announcement). The right option paraphrases instead of repeating: „hat Verspätung“ → „ist nicht pünktlich“, „Die Abfahrt ist … an Gleis fünf“ → „Er fährt von Gleis fünf“. Re-teach: dialogue lines 2, 3, 7 and 9.

Proof goal 3 (say where I am going): one part. A bus driver asks „Wohin fahren Sie?“ and the ticket (Bremen – Berlin) is data: „Ich fahre nach Berlin.“, also with heute, „mit dem Bus“ or „von Bremen“, and the short „(Von Bremen) nach Berlin.“ „in Berlin“, „zu Berlin“, „Ich gehe nach Berlin.“ and a bare „Berlin.“ fail. LIMIT: nobody says „Ich fahre …“ in the Lektion 10 dialogue, the Wortfeld examples or the pool (only notice.formExamples has „Wir fahren nach Österreich.“). The re-teach pointer is line 0, which models „nach Österreich“ and nothing more; the short answer „Nach Berlin.“ can be built from it.

Proof, limits of the engine that hold for every task of this Lektion: (1) A standalone „Entschuldigung!“, „Danke!“ or „Guten Tag!“ before or after the answer counts as an extra sentence and fails. proofTasks() takes the free courtesies from this Lektion’s Wortfeld only (src/lib/lesson/proof.js, `courtesies`), and Danke, Bitte and Entschuldigung are Lektion 1 entries, so here none is free. (2) Any other extra sentence fails as well, also a correct one. (3) A name added to the answer fails („Lena, …“, „…, Paul?“, „Herr Schmidt, …“); the engine removes only a final „, Herr/Frau X“ of a titled speaker of this dialogue. So the prompts use partners without a name. (4) A dot inside a clock time („9.00 Uhr“) splits the answer into two sentences. (5) The notice cannot be a re-teach pointer: its bodyDe fails RULE 35’s word horizon. (6) By microphone the engine scores against the one canonical `answer`, so another accepted form may score low when spoken (read from ProofStage.jsx and answerProof(), not tested).
